chapter: Bill Robinson and Chuck and Chuckles
title: Becoming friends with Bojangles: pool for tap steps and Uncle Bill
summary: Robinson recognises Green from the gaming room, they play pool where each ball pocketed means a tap step, and Robinson teaches him the 32 bars.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: This is Tape Number Twelve of Chuck Green.
Yeah, well, as I was saying, Mr. Bill

Bojangles Robinson, how we became friends. He asked me, he says, "I like you. I like the way you talk. Who are you? Who is your father? Who is your mother? Who is your sister? Who is your brother? Where are you from? Do you play pool?" Said, "Seems like I know you." "What do they call you?" So I told him, "Well, they used to call me Shorty." I said, "I remember you from that night at the gaming room." He laughed and said, "Oh, yeah. You was that pool shooter there's partner. You was with this same man that was leading his orchestra now Don Redmond." I said, "Yeah. Yeah." He said, "You know it's my birthday, my birthday today." He says, "And I'm quite sure I sent my valet to invite you to have a slice of the cake, you know. Well, you're going to have a slice of cake with me, aren't you? Wish me a happy birthday." I said, "Well, I guess so, sure. Sure enough." He says, "Say, look here, do you still shoot pool like you did with that Don Redmond?" And so I explained to Mr. Bojangles that night. I said, "Well, during the time that you challenged us I was just getting ready to take another pool lesson, and that's why he chose me as his partner." So, he laughed again. He said, "Well, you know, I'm not supposed to do anything but happy things during this week. How would you like to go out with me and we'll go and get some ice cream, and we go and go to some pool room and shoot some pool?" Said, "You know, that's my sport. I like that, you know. I'm known as a sport, you

know." So we did. Now, when we gets there, he said, "I'll tell you what. We'll play a," -- he said, "I like the way you tap dance you know. I was looking for you to do some of my tap dance, but I noticed I didn't see any," he said. "But I like the way you tap dance." He said, "I'll tell you, we'll play pool, say, whatever ball that we pocket, that's how many tap steps you'd have to do." So I said, "Yes, sir. Well, what are we going to call the game?" And he said, "We'll call it New America." So I did. I loved his tap dancing, so I was hoping I could get him to do -- make the highest number of balls, you see. He'd have to do that many tap steps. He didn't notice at first, but eventually he caught on. He said, "What are you, trying to learn yourself some of my tap dancing?" He said, "Well, look here, I want to teach you some of my tap steps. I think I know your favorites." And that's how I learned how to do that 32 bars of tap steps, you see, that I demonstrated earlier for you. We became great friends. He wants to adopt me. He wants me to be like his nephew. And I'm supposed to call him Uncle Bill. He said, "Wouldn't you like to call me Uncle Bill?" And I said, "Well, I can't call you Uncle Bill. I've already got an uncle." And he said, "Yeah? What's his name?" I said, "John W. Bubbles." "Oh, Buck and Bubbles. That's right. That's where you all, Slim and Shorty, came from Buck and Bubbles." He laughed again. He said, "All right. We won't fall out over that." And we

remained friends, but as I said, the show was only playing there, he was only appearing a week, he was there with us. He was on a personal appearance tour, so we done that week together. Like to have got held over, you see, but the show had to move on. Happy go lucky from there.
